Executive Summary Globally, solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) supply chains are dominated by products manufactured in China and elsewhere by Chinese companies. However, the recent growth of U.S. PV and BESS manufacturing is bolstering energy security via domestic supply chains that create U.S. manufacturing jobs. This report analyzes U.S. PV and BESS supply chains and costs in 2024 for PV module and battery technologies, structural and electrical balance of system (BOS) components, and PV recycling. The report concludes with an analysis of technology installation trends, government support for domestic manufacturing, manufacturing jobs, and the domestic content of PV systems installed in the United States in 2024. Figure ES-1 summarizes the report’s analysis of U.S. PV and BESS supply chains in 2024, showing the most vulnerability in the crystalline- silicon (c-Si) module and BESS supply chains, with stronger supply chains for cadmium telluride (CdTe) modules and structural and electrical BOS components. U.S. Market and Policies in 2024 In 2024, 47.1 GW direct current (GW )of PV was installed in the United States, bringing total dc installations to 224.1 GW , which accounted for 7% of U.S. electricity generation. About 67% dc of the U.S. PV installed in 2024 was in utility-scale systems using single-axis tracking systems and large, bifacial c-Si (mostly passivated emitter and rear cell, or PERC) modules, with another 16% in utility-scale systems using CdTe modules. The remaining PV capacity mainly consisted of residential systems (mostly smaller PERC modules and module-level power electronics [MLPE] including microinverters and dc optimizers), with the balance installed in commercial systems (ground-mount and rooftop) and utility-scale systems using fixed-tilt racking. PV systems are increasingly being physically paired or brought online with BESS technologies, which typically provide 1–6 hours of energy storage, compensating for the variability of PV generation. Between 2020 and 2024, U.S. BESS installations grew more than tenfold to 96.0 GWh (33.6 GW alternating current [GW ]), including 31.1 GWh (12.3 GW ) installed in 2024 ac ac (Masson, Van Rechem, et al. 2025). Together, PV and BESS represented 84% of new U.S. electricity capacity additions in 2024. Many trade policies and domestic incentives in place in 2024 were designed to impact the supply chains behind U.S. PV and BESS installations. To illustrate historical trends, Figure ES-2 shows U.S. production of PV components between 2007 and 2024. The U.S. Department of Commerce determined that the steep drop in U.S. module production between 2011 and 2012 was due to competition from low-price Chinese modules (U.S. Federal Register 2011).
